Squint: L15 'Five things a good plan has' and L23 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' each name their concept with the numeral as a nav-rail handle (`check_writing.md §20`'s 2026-08-22 header carve-out names both of these headers verbatim as keepers). Truth clause, closest line: L35 'What you can test and check sets your complexity ceiling' is an unqualified universal about capability, and it is exactly what L42-43 license — 'Push reach past what you can check and you have not delegated more. You are checking less.' and 'The ceiling is not fixed.' No dropped qualifier and no category error: the header names the relationship between the two axes, which IS the model, and maintainer L47 records the deliberate choice to keep the model's NAME off the header at M2 so `the-gate-is-a-claim.md` stays the naming beat.

In one sentence: the student leaves this lecture holding a rubric and an appetite — 'I know what to look for' — which is anticipation aimed AT M2's grounded competence, and it sets up `push-back-on-the-plan` by giving the exercise something to hold a plan against. That matches both the strategy doc's M2 mood ('grounded competence — I can feel when a plan is good before approving it') and the file's own Meta at L76-77 ('Mood target: anticipation toward grounded competence... the payoff of *actually feeling it* lands in the exercise'). Regenerated trace: single teaching phase 8/10, close 8/10, is_me 8/10, none below the 8 floor, no beat scored as setup-exempt (slide 1 is a live-do teaching beat, not plumbing — it cannot be compressed to a parenthetical without losing the fact the student's own agent supplies). Beat carrying the mood hardest is L32, the deferral bullet: 'What the plan doesn't decide, the agent decides mid-run... you will not notice.'

Line closest to punitive is L27: 'The plan matches what you'd have written, which feels like alignment. But it was written from a partial read of the codebase, and your instinct is not a check on it. Read it assuming something in there is wrong; there usually is.' It stays epistemic because the defect is located in the PLAN and in the agent's partial read, not in the student's competence — 'your instinct is not a check on it' denies a method its evidentiary status rather than accusing the reader of having erred. Nothing in the file is retrospective about work the student has already shipped; the whole surface is a not-yet-approved artefact, so there is no done-wrong to be ashamed of. Same register at L26 ('reasonable steps in the wrong order... still ship a bug') — the bug is the plan's, not the reader's.

No failure word in the H1, and no remedy is named in a header that the body does not teach.
